answer.rationale: With the line at 94% of committed volume, no buffer, and 14 days to expiry, switching primary vendors (memory_c2) or adding a second source (memory_c3) introduces delivery risk this cycle and neither can be safely executed in the window. The incumbent has refused to reopen price, but memory_c4 indicates the incumbent moved on both price and payment terms when benchmarked — I want to verify that record before relying on it, since the stated refusal appears to contradict it. Negotiating terms (payment terms, volume-tier pricing for next cycle, escalation caps) is the only lever that can reduce TCO without touching supply continuity. Renewal itself must happen regardless to avoid a lapse; the negotiation is attached to that renewal. If verification of memory_c4 undermines the benchmarking lever, I would fall back to a short renewal with a scheduled renegotiation and second-source qualification next cycle.
